extracted.intended_audience: professionals and decisionmakers in government, business, NGOs, and academia; prospective E&E News subscribers
extracted.subtask_description: A subscription landing / homepage describing E&E News's standards, coverage scope, and subscriber benefits for energy and environment journalism aimed at professional audiences.

rubrics_metrics.name: Timeliness
rubrics_metrics.description: Provides 'timely' reporting and 'late-breaking news' so readers 'never miss a beat.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Emphasizes prompt coverage and alerts (e.g., 'Don’t Miss a Beat', 'Late-breaking news', email alerts). Timeliness is signaled by frequent posting times on articles and phrases like 'maximiz[e] your impact with timely ... reporting.'

rubrics_metrics.name: In-depth and original reporting
rubrics_metrics.description: Delivers 'in-depth' journalism that is 'original and investigative,' producing compelling content beyond headlines.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Claims of 'original and investigative reporting' and 'compelling content' imply long-form, reporting-driven work and exclusive reporting examples; intended to include investigative pieces and original reporting not available elsewhere.

rubrics_metrics.name: Objectivity and accuracy
rubrics_metrics.description: Committed to providing 'objective, in-depth, and insightful journalism' that is 'accurate, timely, and unbiased.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Editorial standard emphasizes unbiased treatment of issues ('objective and trusted'), accuracy and insight; used as an evaluative claim about stories and newsroom practices.

rubrics_metrics.name: Relevance to professional audiences
rubrics_metrics.description: Coverage is tailored to 'professionals' and 'top decisionmakers in government, business, NGOs and academia' and aims to keep them 'informed and ahead of the curve.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Stories are positioned to support policymaking and professional decisions; relevance includes policy implications, regulatory updates, and items of interest to institutional readers.

rubrics_metrics.name: Topical breadth (policy, science, business, etc.)
rubrics_metrics.description: Covers a broad range of energy and environment topics: 'climate policy, environmental regulations, sustainability, innovations in the energy sector, and more.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Explicit topic pillars listed ('Policy. Science. Business. Congress. Legislation. Politics.') indicate breadth across technical, policy, and business domains; useful for evaluating completeness of coverage.

rubrics_metrics.name: Frequency and consistency of output
rubrics_metrics.description: Regular, high-volume publication (e.g., '~25 original stories published daily' across 'five daily publications').
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Frequency metrics signal consistent coverage cadence; 'five daily publications' and per-article timestamps demonstrate ongoing, repeated reporting as part of quality and timeliness.

rubrics_metrics.name: Editorial expertise and credibility
rubrics_metrics.description: Staffed by experienced reporters ('65+ energy and environment reporters'), with long-standing institutional experience ('25 years of journalism') and strong subscriber retention ('90% subscriber retention rate').
rubrics_metrics.guidance: These staff and longevity metrics are presented as evidence of authority and trustworthiness; they function as criteria for judging the outlet's reliability and expertise.

rubrics_metrics.name: Subscriber services and exclusives
rubrics_metrics.description: Provides subscriber-specific features such as 'email alerts, exclusive documents, and all-access' to in-depth coverage.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Subscription benefits (alerts, exclusive documents, all-access) are part of the product standard — evaluating the offering includes whether subscribers receive these promised services and deliverables.
